paper:1993WtFor...8..281M.takeaway: Separates three kinds of forecast goodness: consistency with the forecaster's true belief, quality as correspondence with observation, and value as the benefit realized by the user, and shows they can move in opposite directions.

paper:2022arXiv221003629Y.takeaway: Interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning with tool actions so a model can plan, query external sources, and self-correct — reducing hallucination on decision tasks.

paper:2023arXiv230212173G.takeaway: Attackers compromise LLM-integrated apps by planting instructions in content the model later retrieves (web pages, documents) — no direct access needed.

paper:2024JAMES..1604019R.takeaway: Defines a common evaluation framework with fixed ground truth, baselines and headline scores across deterministic and probabilistic metrics, and reports every major learned model against operational IFS on the same footing.

paper:2024arXiv240217753M.takeaway: Introduces LoCoMo, the canonical long-term conversational-memory benchmark: very-long dyadic (person-person) dialogues spanning up to ~35 sessions / hundreds of turns, generated via a machine-human pipeline with personas and temporal event graphs, plus a QA test suite, event-summarization, and multimodal-dialogue-generation tasks.

paper:2024arXiv240517974C.takeaway: Surveys 22 personalized-dialogue datasets and 17 seminal works (2021-2023), cataloging persona/personalization datasets, problem types, and evaluation facets/metrics for personalized dialogue.

paper:2024arXiv240601171T.takeaway: Surveys the persona concept across role-playing and personalization, distinguishing how personas are constructed, conditioned, and evaluated in LLMs.

paper:2024arXiv240608467L.takeaway: Over 750 Dafny programs, about 53,000 lines, testing whether a model can supply enough hints for the verifier to succeed.

paper:2024arXiv240611915L.takeaway: A minimal benchmark for proving properties of code in Lean (miniCodeProps).

paper:2024arXiv240613352D.takeaway: A dynamic benchmark of realistic tool-using tasks for measuring prompt-injection attacks and defenses — and showing current defenses are far from complete.

paper:2024arXiv240907429Z.takeaway: Introduces Agent Workflow Memory, inducing reusable workflows from past trajectories to improve long-horizon web-navigation agents, evaluated on agent-trajectory benchmarks (e.g. web tasks) rather than conversational QA.

paper:2024arXiv241010813W.takeaway: Defines LongMemEval, a chat-assistant memory benchmark organized around five core abilities (information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention), with controllable interaction histories so memory load can be scaled independently of the target evidence.

paper:2024arXiv241202980H.takeaway: Proposes evaluating synthetic-data generators by the Quality–Diversity–Complexity (QDC) makeup of their output, finding quality drives in-distribution generalization, diversity drives OOD generalization, and complexity helps both — with explicit quality–diversity trade-offs.

paper:2025JGRH....2..496U.takeaway: Sets out what an evaluation has to include before a learned Earth-system model can be trusted: physical consistency checks, out-of-sample and out-of-distribution testing, and independence between the developers and the evaluators.

paper:2025arXiv250107278Z.takeaway: Roadmap framing continual/incremental learning for LLM agents, organizing memory, forgetting, and knowledge-accumulation challenges.

paper:2025arXiv250205714D.takeaway: Formally verified code generation over competitive-programming problems in Lean (FVAPPS).

paper:2025arXiv250211127W.takeaway: Detects anomalies over the agent communication graph and intervenes to defend a multi-agent system against attacks that propagate between agents.

paper:2025arXiv250212110X.takeaway: Zettelkasten-style self-organizing agent memory with dynamic linking and note evolution as new memories arrive.

paper:2025arXiv250213270L.takeaway: Releases REALTALK, 21 days of genuine human-human messaging conversations (not LLM-synthesized), used to study long-term memory probing and persona/emotional-intelligence simulation against the distribution gap between synthetic and real dialogue.

paper:2025arXiv250214847H.takeaway: Injects malicious messages that propagate through inter-agent communication channels, compromising a multi-agent system from the inside.

paper:2025arXiv250218418W.takeaway: The first reranker trained to spend test-time compute: distills R1/o1 reasoning traces so a small model reasons before scoring relevance.

paper:2025arXiv250304779L.takeaway: Evaluates LLM reasoning about program semantics through formal specification inference (FormalBench).

paper:2025arXiv250312029C.takeaway: Structured multi-agent debate yields minimal-to-inconsistent gains over a strong single-agent baseline on software-engineering tasks.

paper:2025arXiv250313657C.takeaway: 14 failure modes in 3 categories — specification issues, inter-agent misalignment, task verification — built with an LLM-as-judge pipeline at Cohen's κ=0.88.

paper:2025arXiv250322458G.takeaway: PRISMA-based survey of evaluation methods for LLM agents in multi-turn conversational settings, cataloging benchmarks, metrics, and methodologies across the multi-turn evaluation landscape.

paper:2025arXiv250323278H.takeaway: Surveys the security threat landscape of MCP — the tool-connection standard now powering most agentic systems — and its expanding attack surface.

paper:2025arXiv250403947S.takeaway: Distills then RL-refines reasoning into a 3B reranker that generates relevance explanations at inference; third on BRIGHT, beating 20x-larger models.

paper:2025arXiv250408000L.takeaway: Per-neuron stability/plasticity balancing to address the stability-plasticity dilemma in deep RL agents.

paper:2025arXiv250513938T.takeaway: A curated benchmark for formally verified code generation with human-checked ground truth (CLEVER).

paper:2025arXiv250519271D.takeaway: Requires code, specification and proof to be produced at once, following the VerifyThis competition format.

paper:2025arXiv250523135Y.takeaway: Benchmarks verifiable code generation on Lean tasks that require code, specification and proof together, each graded separately (VERINA).

paper:2025arXiv250922908B.takeaway: A benchmark for vericoding: formally verified program synthesis from specifications.

paper:2025arXiv251006296Z.takeaway: Scores formally verifiable code by equivalence rather than against a reference solution (VeriEquivBench).

paper:2025arXiv251023350C.takeaway: Validates formal specifications with LLM-generated test cases.

paper:2025arXiv251115403A.takeaway: Applies mutation testing to Dafny specifications to reveal weaknesses in the specifications themselves (MutDafny).

paper:2026arXiv260209464Z.takeaway: An aligned benchmark for verified code generation on classical algorithms (AlgoVeri).

paper:2026arXiv260318334X.takeaway: Evaluates Rust verification through the chain of reasoning rather than binary pass or fail on proof hints (VCoT-Bench).

paper:2026arXiv260408064Q.takeaway: Proposes ImplicitMemBench to measure implicit (procedural) memory, where past experience becomes automated behavior, rather than the explicit fact-recall that existing memory benchmarks test.

paper:2026arXiv260408362C.takeaway: Introduces OmniBehavior, the first user-simulation benchmark built entirely from real-world traces, and uses it to show LLM simulators converge to a 'positive average person' (hyper-activity, persona homogenization, Utopian bias), losing individual differences and long-tail behaviors.

paper:2026arXiv260408988J.takeaway: Benchmark moving beyond episodic task scoring to evaluate self-evolving agents across time, targeting 'episodic amnesia' and static-toolset limits.

paper:2026arXiv260411182Z.takeaway: Argues existing memory benchmarks cover only Person-AI and dyadic Person-Person dialogue and neglects 'continuous dialogue lifelogs' from always-on wearables; introduces lifelog memory evaluation resources (LifeMem / EgoMem first-person scenarios) for ambient continuously-recorded conversation.

paper:2026arXiv260411306B.takeaway: H2-EMV: LM-based relevance estimation drives selective forgetting under learned natural-language rules updated by user feedback; measures QA accuracy retention against memory-size and query-compute savings.

paper:2026arXiv260411544W.takeaway: Encodes time as continuous phase rotation (not a discrete label) in temporal KG / agentic memory so validity intervals and obsolescence are representable.

paper:2026arXiv260411557L.takeaway: A unified tool-learning pipeline that builds a 22k+ tool pool and 390k+ instances by combining 10 public datasets with structurally controlled synthetic trajectories (single/multi-hop, single/multi-turn, serial/parallel), adds an Anchor Linkage mechanism for cross-turn dependencies, and a QAOA evaluation representation.

paper:2026arXiv260411563G.takeaway: Pins down LoCoMo's exact composition (ACL 2024 version: 10 conversations, 1,813 questions) and argues every LoCoMo system treats memory as retrieval over dialogue segments while none reports adversarial robustness (refusing questions about facts never disclosed); proposes that abstention/hallucination-resistance metric as a missing axis.

paper:2026arXiv260411767L.takeaway: Well-formedness / termination guarantees for agent composition via a typed calculus.

paper:2026arXiv260412179M.takeaway: Presents a topic-guided multi-agent conversation-generation pipeline that synthesizes dialogues specifically for fine-tuning and evaluating both short- and long-term memory.

paper:2026arXiv260412376L.takeaway: Evicts old content past the context window but indexes it with keyword bookmarks so the model can recover evicted memory on demand.

paper:2026arXiv260413085K.takeaway: Liquid-Glass-Crystal three-phase consolidation governed by an Itô SDE / Fokker-Planck (closed-form Beta stationary dist.); proves convergence + memory-capacity bounds and empirically reports forward transfer and forgetting reductions.

paper:2026arXiv260420382M.takeaway: Generates clinically grounded synthetic multi-turn counseling dialogues from structured client psychological graphs, encoding the underlying clinical reasoning rather than just masking real utterances, to sidestep confidentiality constraints on real data.

paper:2026arXiv260420943S.takeaway: Memory architecture drawing on neuroscientific sleep-consolidation principles, pairing offline consolidation with an explicit algorithmic-forgetting operator to bound store growth.

paper:2026arXiv260421229A.takeaway: A synthetic long-term memory benchmark of 5 personas, 100 multi-session conversations, and 150 queries spanning factual recall, cross-space integration, temporal reasoning, adversarial abstention, and emergent synthesis, holding the answering model fixed (GPT-4o) to isolate memory architecture.

paper:2026arXiv260422085M.takeaway: Typed semantic memory using information-theoretic retrieval scoring to govern what is retained/surfaced across sessions for long-horizon agents.

paper:2026arXiv260423424H.takeaway: Teacher-compiled persistent knowledge store refined through sleep consolidation and usage-driven retention/decay for small local LMs.

paper:2026arXiv260423459H.takeaway: The same task under different multi-agent architectures has different security properties.

paper:2026arXiv260423878B.takeaway: Replaces system-engineering memory metaphors (paging/flat stores) with a 7-layer neuroscience-grounded architecture incorporating consolidation and forgetting layers.

paper:2026arXiv260424977N.takeaway: A dedicated survey organizing the design space of LLM-based conversational user simulators (persona conditioning, goal/intent modeling, behavioral realism, evaluation of simulators themselves).

paper:2026arXiv260440441M.takeaway: A configurable simulation framework that injects realistic patient 'noise' (incomplete, inconsistent, distracting user behavior) into evaluation, exposing that strong static-benchmark scores collapse under realistic interaction.

paper:2026arXiv260501394X.takeaway: A live benchmark of agentic workflows on specification generation (LiveFMBench).

paper:2026arXiv260501399P.takeaway: A verbal reranker that reasons in natural language to bridge retrieval and the generator, instead of injecting raw passages.

paper:2026arXiv260503356Z.takeaway: Benchmarks formal postcondition inference on both correctness and completeness rather than correctness alone.

paper:2026arXiv260506527C.takeaway: Benchmark of 400 expert-validated conflict scenarios / 1,200 queries (contexts to 150K tokens) probing belief revision over time via three dimensions: State Resolution, Premise Resistance, Implicit Policy Adaptation; introduces 'Implicit Conflict' failure mode and CUPMem write-time-revision baseline.

paper:2026arXiv260507935X.takeaway: Uses TLA+ counterexamples to repair coordination protocols.

paper:2026arXiv260509100M.takeaway: Unifies reasoning-driven generation, retrieval, and compression in one LLM, sharing training across embedding and generative tasks.

paper:2026arXiv260511026R.takeaway: Plants deception traps (fake tools/credentials) that detect indirect-prompt-injection compromises which slip past prevention — cross-lingual, near-zero false positives.

paper:2026arXiv260513941L.takeaway: Self-evolving memory that treats retrieval infrastructure as mutable, auto-researching its own organization across multi-session operation.

paper:2026arXiv260514460L.takeaway: Semantic Compliance Hijacking (SCH) weaponizes third-party Agent Skill files without any embedded code: it injects obfuscated natural-language 'compliance guidelines' that the agent's retrieve-contextualize-execute pipeline fuses directly into the LLM system prompt as authoritative directives, and the agent then synthesizes and runs the malicious logic itself at runtime (dumping os.environ and POSTing it as 'telemetry', or exec()-ing a fetched remote byte stream). Across 600 contextualized tasks over 3 frameworks (OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex) and 3 models, SCH hit a peak 77.67% complete-leakage rate and 67.33% RCE, yet both SkillScan (AST/regex) and LLM Guard (semantic classifiers) flagged it at 0.00%, versus 62.00-96.00% detection for SkillJect and 91.61-99.81% for DDIPE explicit-payload baselines; an 'Alignment-Security Paradox' made the most-aligned model (GPT-5.4 mini, 62.11% avg complete leakage) the most exploitable because it best maps prose directives to concrete system APIs.

paper:2026arXiv260514498Y.takeaway: Introduces GroupMemBench, targeting memory in multi-party (group) conversations where the agent must attribute facts to specific speakers across many participants, a setting that dyadic benchmarks like LoCoMo/LongMemEval do not cover.

paper:2026arXiv260514906R.takeaway: Introduces MemLens to benchmark long-term memory in vision-language models across long multimodal interactions, evaluating whether memory methods preserve evidence needed for later recall.

paper:2026arXiv260515128G.takeaway: Proposes MemEye, a visual-centric evaluation framework that specifically tests whether agents preserve the visual evidence required for later recall in multimodal memory.

paper:2026arXiv260517596S.takeaway: Neuro-symbolic, self-curating memory where symbolic structure governs update/curation of persistent cross-session user knowledge.

paper:2026arXiv260526352L.takeaway: Critic-free policy optimization that turns retrieval interactions into localized credit signals for latent reasoning steps.

paper:2026arXiv260526457A.takeaway: An agentic environment for evaluating specification autoformalization in Verus (Verus-SpecGym).

paper:2026arXiv260526563W.takeaway: RootSE distills 93 real repository-level agent failures (over 4,500 execution steps) into a diagnosis benchmark whose target is the earliest decisive error step - the single early mistake, such as a misread requirement or flawed plan, whose cumulative consequence is the eventual system failure.

paper:2026arXiv260526667G.takeaway: Builds a stress-test benchmark that systematically enumerates and probes failure modes of external memory systems (consistency breaks over long-horizon interactions) rather than aggregate accuracy.

paper:2026arXiv260530087Y.takeaway: Constructs a diagnostic testbed for selective QA over conflicting multi-source personal memory, where the system must decide how to use contradictory stored facts, plus a comparison of methods on that testbed.

paper:2026arXiv260601317H.takeaway: The attack surface is the whole readable workspace, not the prompt. SABER separates three causal origins: 289 tasks hide malicious instructions in project artifacts such as build metadata or dependency manifests (70.1% HSR, with 23.0% of effective runs showing multi-step compositional harm), 186 tasks are entirely benign requests where an unsafe shortcut is available (68.3% HSR with no adversary present at all), and 241 tasks put safety-relevant warnings in the workspace (82.5% HSR, the worst split). Cause labels put operational misunderstanding at 47.7% of harmful runs, ahead of injection-following at 25.4% and harmful-operation compliance at 25.1%. Capability does not buy safety: DeepSeek-V3.2 exceeds V3 at 79.6% vs 72.4% HSR while being less incapable, and Qwen3.5 moves only from 78.6% at 9B to 73.4% at 397B.

paper:2026arXiv260607682D.takeaway: A 5-bucket failure taxonomy over 526 agent-attributable failures: implementation failure (41.6%) and timeout (31.4%) dominate, then reward hacking (15.4%), premature termination (7.6%), and poor self-verification (4.0%); long context degrades behavior actively — pass rate falls monotonically with consecutive-duplicate run length (claude-code 41.9%→3.2%) and compaction/summarizer trials pass at 0% vs 8.9% without.

paper:2026arXiv260609900W.takeaway: The read path retrieves through four channels in parallel — dense semantic, BM25 lexical, graph n-hop from query entities, and recency/salience — fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then applies an 'as-of' filter and an abstention gate; the assembled context is hybrid (conflict-resolved facts plus raw session chunks) because facts alone lose recall.

paper:2026arXiv260610388D.takeaway: Retrieved skills enter the agent as procedural context before planning or execution, which makes the retrieval layer a trust boundary rather than a ranking problem. The paper measures that boundary with harmful sibling rate (HSR@K), the top-K exposure of a query-specific sibling that shares the capability family but would steer execution toward a stale resource, a skipped precondition or the wrong check. Generic lexical retrieval, SkillRouter and BGE reranking recover the helpful skill while exposing the risky sibling; an attribution-listwise method suppresses exposure but loses helpful retrieval quality. The reference method, SkillResolve, reaches Recall@3 0.766 and NDCG@3 0.699 with HSR@3 at 0 under the released family relation, improving on SkillRouter by 0.112 Recall@3 and 0.165 NDCG@3 while dropping its HSR@3 from 0.693. Ablating representative selection under the same scorer raises HSR@3 to 0.236, so exposure is controlled by the within-family choice and not by the scorer.

paper:2026arXiv260610616K.takeaway: Frames retention/eviction as a constrained multi-step stochastic optimization over a hard storage budget, with the per-step reward explicitly charging miss penalties, reacquisition delay, and stale-information use; the learned policy keeps a smaller, evidence-denser set rather than greedily filling the budget (LoCoMo budget 128: F1 0.302 at 0.76 occupancy vs Mixed-Score 0.069 at 0.99).

paper:2026arXiv260610677J.takeaway: At read time an agentic procedure lets the LLM iteratively call memory tools — inspect intermediate results, expand local context around matches, assemble evidence — rather than take a single top-k step; the agentic variant beats a hybrid summary+BM25 reader (79.3% vs 76.0% on LongMemEval_S).

paper:2026arXiv260614470S.takeaway: Separates the value of a substrate from raw accuracy: per-backend cost is measured, and a similarity sweep shows memory pays only above a 'copyability threshold' — when the retrieved case is a near-duplicate (cosine ≳ 0.8) accuracy jumps +12 to +13.5 pp, while below it nothing helps; the gain is answer retrieval, not method transfer, and a 4.5× larger backbone steepens the near-duplicate step (+22.5 to +28.5 pp) yet still cannot extract a transferable method from a worked example.

paper:2026arXiv260614571L.takeaway: A streaming benchmark sourced from real EgoLife egocentric lifelogs rather than scripted or synthesized dialogue: each five-minute segment is mined for a hidden 'evidence anchor' (a user-specific preference, plan, or capability) that spawns a two-step task sequence — an initial task that needs the evidence and a follow-up task grounded in the same anchor; eight memory systems are evaluated across two backbones (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Gemini-3-Flash).

paper:2026arXiv260614790L.takeaway: The paper makes the failure taxonomy explicit before scaling fan-out: a single agent's hallucinated/malformed/misinterpreted output becomes shared state and corrupts downstream decisions. Concrete failure modes observed: tau3-bench baseline reaches the right end state via an invalid path (treats a parameter clarification as authorization to mutate); CorpusQA fails on the interpretation rule not the retrieved value; SWE-bench baseline submits a patch after local validation already failed. The cloud-edge fan-out is gated: edge workers see only assigned chunks, write only declared outputs, and must pass schema + coverage checks before entering global state.

paper:2026arXiv260615405G.takeaway: T-Mem retrieves through a top-down topic -> scene -> item cascade, scoring each layer with reciprocal rank fusion over both a shared BM25 lexical index and a per-type dense index (bge-m3). On top of these node indices, four write-time 'trigger' families surface host nodes on the query's behalf: items expose three independently-encoded views (concept-only, bridge-only, joint) and the trigger score is the nan-aware max across views, attributed back to the host item. Scenes/items reached through associative triggers bypass the topic prefilter, because gating them by surviving topics would re-impose the similarity-only neighbourhood the system is built to escape.

paper:2026arXiv260617016X.takeaway: Lifecycle-Aware Eviction tracks each context segment through three states active -> completed -> evictable, gated on evidence that a sub-task achieved its objective and on residual utility. A completed segment is not immediately purged; it retains its physical cache slots as long as residual relevance to ongoing interactions is non-zero, and only an evictable segment (utility decayed to zero) is removed in a single-pass structural purge. State estimation runs via a lightweight zero-shot validator over a compressed historical view in conservative batches of B turns rather than every step.

paper:2026arXiv260617328L.takeaway: MemTrace contains 835 typed knowledge points drawn from 20 users, expanded into 15,422 question rows and over 200,000 scored answers, and is used to evaluate 13 memory-system configurations spanning four paradigms: long-context models, retrieval-augmented systems, external-memory stores, and agentic-memory architectures.

paper:2026arXiv260619380G.takeaway: Decomposes non-adversarial coding-agent failure into three sequential points — forming the correct target (underspecification), pursuing it (capability error), and executing it through the harness (stochastic sampling, context decay) — with a chain-rule risk P(unsafe)=1-(1-f1)(1-f2)(1-f3) and scenarios that isolate each stage, cross-cut by four active modes (greenfield, editing, deployment, monitoring) over 8 scenarios, 20 environments, and 59 transcript templates at n>=500 across three frontier models.

paper:2026arXiv260622504S.takeaway: PORTICO is a reference monitor that gives coding-agent tools a bounded capability lifetime: an explicit task contract compiles into an initial envelope plus grant, trusted-closure, and global-deny rules, and a request-grant-invoke protocol mints opaque, epoch-bound handles that are revoked when the subgoal closes, so authority cannot linger or be replayed once its justifying episode ends.

paper:2026arXiv260622673L.takeaway: A white-box runtime defense for multi-turn coding agents that drive a shell in Docker. At each step it reads the last-token hidden state at one layer and runs a single linear probe to flag a harmful execution state; on a flag it steers the representation inside a sparse 10-dimensional subspace, adapting only the steering strength via an LLM judge scoring safety (0.6) and utility (0.4). It detects current-step risk at 97.32% average accuracy, predicts the next harmful command at up to 96.77% lookahead, and cuts average attack success from 85.99% to 13.36% (72.63 pp), beating RepE and self-reminder. Negative steering of the same subspace flips genuine refusals into malicious commands (100% ASR on LLaMA), confirming the direction is causal not lexical; under prompt injection the probe misfires but applying the steering direction still drops ASR 86.7%->6.7%.

paper:2026arXiv260622678B.takeaway: Names a failure taxonomy for the lab-to-production gap — fragile fixes (patches pass tests but leave latent bugs), token waste (trial-and-error instead of a planned approach), false confidence (never abstaining on impossible/ambiguous tasks), and broken intermediates (codebase left broken between steps). Baseline ReAct agents fail badly against it: no baseline abstained on any of the 6 impossible tasks, and even disciplined agents abstained correctly only 62% of the time. Recovery is the hardest mode and the one scaffolding does NOT fix — smallest gain of all five pillars, token-waste cut only 34%, doom loops persist when root cause isn't in the error message; the authors conclude recovery may need architectural changes beyond configuration-level frameworks.

paper:2026arXiv260625449K.takeaway: Separates two regimes that look identical from outside: anchoring (the source is still in context and a directed correction works) and information loss (the source is gone and reclaim is 0.00 by measurement, checkable as a token test on the carried note); the wall and the source-first fix replicate across three deployed memory systems and on MultiWOZ dialogue.

paper:2026arXiv260626511Y.takeaway: Across four marker-free evolving benchmarks (code mutation, config migration, dependency bumps, API evolution), plain RAG serves the superseded value 15-40% of the time when forced to answer; MemStrata drives this to ~0% via deterministic supersession rather than any decay or scoring-based forgetting heuristic.

paper:2026arXiv260626721Z.takeaway: KPR treats an external collaborator's code, tests, and agent trace as a knowledge source, not a merge candidate; only a project-owned inner trusted coding agent regenerates code inside the receiving project's environment, under repository context and security policy, before anything can be merged.

paper:2026arXiv260626806H.takeaway: Frames consolidation on the complementary-learning-systems analogy (fast episodic plus slow consolidating stores) but states it is motivation only, not a biological model. Consolidation is measured by write economy and bounded drift, not task accuracy: EVAF reaches goal persistence and post-unload recovery of 0.812–0.904 with only 2–3 parametric writes per 200 events (L2 drift ~21–29), while Naive-LoRA writes every event (200 writes, L2 drift ~67 on TinyLlama, ~119 on GPT-2) and still fails the goal layer — so writing everything is not enough. Stability-plasticity is handled with replay plus an L2/EWC-style anchor. The unresolved boundary is stale-memory obsolescence: on public Memora event streams EVAF improves forgetting-absence only 91/222 to 95/222 (McNemar p=0.57, not significant), and negative-gradient/anti-training forgetting variants were unstable — append-only selective consolidation does not solve delete/update validity.

paper:2026arXiv260627243L.takeaway: NOVA's verification cascade checks architecture semantics before expensive training or deployment, catching runnable-but-structurally-invalid candidates that pass unit tests but violate recommender-specific invariants like sequence masking; failed-verification diagnostics become reusable 'forbidden directions' that shape later search.

paper:2026arXiv260627416P.takeaway: Glite ARF enforces task-level worktree isolation and immutability with a corrections overlay after an incident where one agent step recomputed and corrupted 20,304 historical training rows across 38 feature sets; completed task folders can't be modified, so fixes are separate, auditable downstream tasks.

paper:2026arXiv260628235R.takeaway: Across 930,000+ agent-authored pull requests, multilevel models show about half the variance in integration friction survives after accounting for the contribution, its author, size, and agent, and it is a repository-level property. Agent-authored contributions concentrate this repository-level friction roughly twice as much as human ones (ICC 0.30 vs 0.16).

paper:2026arXiv260701071X.takeaway: MemSyco-Bench covers five task categories testing whether agents can reject memory as factual evidence, respect its scope, resolve memory-vs-evidence conflicts, track updates, and use valid memory for personalization, built after showing existing benchmarks (LongMemEval, LoCoMo, STALE, PersonaMem) put 47.4-66.1% of their errors in the retrieval-failure bucket versus only 5.8-13.7% in the post-retrieval-reasoning bucket.

paper:2026arXiv260702436M.takeaway: Ninety independent agent runs build the same real-time retrospective board from one specification, scored on a 14-criterion rubric worth 42 points. Raising reasoning effort from High to xHigh on Opus 4.7 lifts first-try perfect runs from 5 of 18 to 16 of 18, a 61-point difference with a 95% interval of 29 to 78, and cuts corrective prompts from 0.89 to 0.17 per run. Giving the agent a Playwright browser-testing tool does not change the score. Docker deployment fails on the first try in 40 of 90 runs, and two environment criteria account for 55 of the 100 first-try criterion failures.

paper:2026arXiv260705076D.takeaway: Evaluates code-derived and LLM-written specifications on a production point-of-sale payment workflow, grading them against traces captured from the running system.

paper:2026arXiv260708028A.takeaway: Governance holds only because it is code-owned, not prompted. With the model fixed and only the enforcement layer varied, prompt instructions alone let recommendation-language and internal-trace-leakage violations reach the reader on all 30 adversarial runs, every one of which the harness blocked; only source-backed claims are allowed to enter runtime context in the first place. Across 270 composition-boundary runs under three substituted models the contracts held, with failures confined to the model-composed side and recorded.

paper:2026arXiv260710059L.takeaway: The paper gives an agent-native failure taxonomy of 8 abstention scenarios, organized by when a trigger becomes observable (pre-execution reasoning vs. runtime discovery) and where it resides (query, environment state, or tools). Across 17 frontier LLMs in 4 harnesses the best agent, Gemini 3.1 Pro, reaches only 59.5% Paired Accuracy and 13 of 17 stay below 50%, and abstention capability tracks largely independently of general task-solving skill. The signature failure is post-hoc abstention: an agent commits an irreversible action, such as cancelling a flight before checking rebooking availability, then verbally acknowledges the problem, leaving unrecoverable side effects.

paper:2026arXiv260712893H.takeaway: A controllably-generated long-horizon conversational-memory benchmark that reformulates memory as five lifecycle operations (remember, forget, update, reflect, and TrajectoryOps that compose events across time), each represented by a gold trace of trigger, target, scope, state transition, and verbatim evidence spans, with six operation-level probe categories evaluated under adjacent-evidence and long-context settings.

paper:2026arXiv260713716W.takeaway: A 96-seed, 384-variant benchmark shows raw-text and first-token approval binding are defeated by wrappers (env, sudo, bash -c, aliases, SDK indirection), while canonical fingerprinting resists wrapper bypass and approval drift; ablating the canonical fingerprint is the single most damaging removal tested, collapsing the retained score to 0.00 since there is no longer a stable object for approval to bind to.

paper:2026arXiv260714890H.takeaway: Treats every agent-emitted lifecycle claim (reviewed, tested, done, ready-to-merge) as inadmissible until fresh, tracked-source-state-bound evidence satisfies a gate. In a 9,240-cell powered ablation, the pre-registered contrast between the gated loop and a compute-budgeted naive loop cut visible-pass/hidden-fail amplification from 31/1,800 injected cells to 2/1,800 (+1.6pp not-amplified, 95% CI [0.8, 2.5]); a near-compute contrast (14/1,800 vs 2/1,800) shows the gain tracks enforcing the review signal as a hard gate, not just adding a reviewer.

paper:2026arXiv260716716S.takeaway: A long-context memory benchmark of 24 investigative case files (criminal, medical, financial), each 50k-100k tokens, with 1,604 questions over six memory-intensive task families: chain reconstruction (locate and causally order 5-15 scattered evidence hops), cascade propagation (after an invalidation, decide which conclusions break and which survive on independent support), source-conflict resolution, counterfactual reasoning, temporal-constraint satisfaction, and temporal fact retrieval as a control. Ground truth is deterministic, built from a provenance DAG, with a fixed question matrix enforcing per-task and per-format quotas across cases.

paper:2026arXiv260717044D.takeaway: Decomposes a production enterprise agent's uplift over its bare base model (+11.0 pp on SpreadsheetBench Verified, +7-10 pp on BullshitBench v2, ~+15 pp on GAIA validation) by architectural layer: scaffolding and prompting account for +9.5 of the +11.0 pp on SpreadsheetBench, while the verification loop's isolated contribution is +1.5 pp (6 rescued tasks) - small but concentrated at the top of the score distribution, where every competitive system has already exhausted scaffolding gains. A specialist-swap ablation shows the loop's value rides on observer independence: moving observe/compare from the small trained verifier back onto the frontier model that generated the artifact cuts SpreadsheetBench rescues from 6 tasks to 2 and drops BullshitBench correct rejection 4-5 pp.

paper:2026arXiv260719407W.takeaway: Benchmarks formal translation across interactive theorem provers (ITPEval).

paper:2026arXiv260720759S.takeaway: Six seed issues from SymPy and requests fan out into 696 adversarial artifacts - four attack categories (installing a disguised PyPI package, planting a hidden executable validation hook that phones an attacker endpoint, poisoning .cursorrules or CLAUDE.md so the agent stops asking for terminal confirmation, and spawning 10,000 worker threads), crossed with six delivery vectors and per-vector perturbations - executed across 6 agent-model configurations for 4,176 runs. 66.5% penetrate both agent- and LLM-level guardrails. Delivery vector is the dominant factor: payloads in ordinary text artifacts (issue bodies, PDFs) succeed in 72.2% of runs against 16.7% when confined to image alt-text, while cross-lingual translation and visual obfuscation show negligible effect. Of 1,400 resisted runs, 82.9% are blocked by the model explicitly refusing and 17.1% by the model classifying the source as untrusted metadata. Spotlighting-style boundary markers failed to stop payload execution.

paper:2026arXiv260723425B.takeaway: Grades natural-language-to-TLA+ generation by running the model checker over the full reachable state space, not by resemblance to a reference (TLA+-Bench).

paper:2026arXiv260725152P.takeaway: The paper names the failure mode, the progress mirage, and defines it as a measurable rate rather than an anecdote: the fraction of evaluator-accepted cycles whose oracle-measured delta is zero or below. The definition was deliberately widened from the preregistered wording of exactly zero, because a delta of zero excludes the worse error of accepting an outright regression. Alongside it the paper reports a wasted-cycle ratio, acceptance rates conditioned separately on non-positive and positive deltas, and time-to-first-positive with right-censoring recorded, all computed mechanically from raw cycle logs with no human discretion. The oracle is a synthetic user simulator kept unreachable by container and network isolation, with a boundary proof run at every run and a canary scan at every cycle, so the ground truth cannot be quietly contaminated by the agent under test. The proposed architecture puts the evaluator in a separate process reading databases, version-control history, web analytics and append-only ledgers, and forces a rejected cycle to leave an artifact the next iteration must read first at boot. Four supporting mechanisms (append-only state, file-based handoff between sessions, periodic frame-adversarial self-review, a self-healing scheduler) are presented as field-derived design notes and are not individually validated.

paper:2026arXiv260728229S.takeaway: The paper is a direct argument against paying for a static embedding index when inference-time reasoning can do the ranking. Librarian maintains no index of its own; it queries Europe PMC's live search and spends LLM calls at request time on query planning and paragraph-level relevance scoring against the question. The authors give four reasons for refusing the dense datastore. It is expensive to build and serve, with OpenScholar's alone at roughly 744 GB. Its margin is narrowing, since a well-tuned BM25 backbone driven by a capable LLM issuing multiple keyword queries now matches or exceeds dense retrieval on scientific benchmarks. Embeddings flatten structured metadata, blocking direct queries over explicit fields such as gene, protein, organism and chemical annotations, which is exactly the structure Europe PMC exposes. And a nearest-neighbour lookup is not inspectable, where a fielded keyword query is. The trade lands: more than 16 points of Citation F1 over strong recent baselines on ScholarQA-Bench, higher expert-consensus agreement as a drop-in retrieval layer, and about 8 points on LitQA2 over web search.

paper:2026arXiv260728802R.takeaway: A taxonomy of 41 agent failure modes that labels each failure with the interaction edge it occurred on (model–context, model–tool, model–memory, and so on) plus a fault side naming the component that owes the repair — the same visible failure (say, an agent reporting a failed tool call as a success) gets a different label depending on whether the tool wrapper suppressed the error or the model ignored it. Labels attach to the earliest failure the trajectory never recovers from, not its downstream symptoms, and four frontier-model judges recover the human labels at up to Cohen's κ = 0.76 (pairwise judge agreement up to 0.84).

paper:2026arXiv260802693W.takeaway: Across six auditor-model systems (OpenCodeReview, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot Code Review, each on two models), splitting an attack across commits barely helps the attacker: decomposition alone moves detection by at most five points. What works is presentation. Interleaving 16 genuine upstream PRs between the malicious ones costs 5-13 points, and fusing each component with a real maintainer diff under a description that coherently accounts for both costs 10-18. The dominant effect is where the benign work sits: from N=0 to N=24 interleaved PRs, per-PR review loses 8-11 points while whole-window review -- the entire release window in one context -- loses 39-45, falling to 16-22% detection against 50-60% under per-PR review. Hiding attack-bearing predecessors from history costs only 4-11 points, so repository history is not the binding constraint; joint occupancy of the auditor's active review context is. Capability mitigates without solving: the strongest configuration still misses 34% of interleaved and 31% of carrier-fused attacks, and with the model held fixed, detection varies 10 points across the three surrounding harnesses.

paper:2026arXiv260802764P.takeaway: The paper's argument for the governance layer is that prompts, evaluations, monitors, and audit logs are empirical or procedural: they can reveal or flag a violation, but none of them defines the invariant that must hold at the moment an operation commits. Policy-as-program systems (Cedar, Microsoft's Agent Governance Toolkit, Omnigent) fix part of this by moving rules out of prompts and application code into reviewable artifacts, but they evaluate at the request boundary, which works for access-control-shaped checks over principal, action, resource, and arguments and breaks for the stateful conditions agent safeguards actually need: refund history, live inventory and holds, cloud quotas, rolling financial limits, risk signals. Provenact keeps the policy artifact and adds a provider contract naming the certified state views and governed effects an operation may use, so enforcement is scoped rather than global. In the scripted, LLM-free procurement workflow, the AGT and Omnigent baselines produce stale authorizations over shared budgets and inventory where Provenact does not, and governance records retain structured decision evidence for audit.

paper:2026arXiv260813077Y.takeaway: Coins scores a candidate specification by instantiating it on trusted test cases and generating concrete proof obligations, so a spec is graded by what it actually rules out.

paper:2026arXiv260813522Y.takeaway: Asks whether agents can build formally verified software repositories, not single functions (Vero).

paper:2026arXiv260813867J.takeaway: A technical monograph synthesizing 164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, and 17 author-system case records through a structured multivocal review, organizing coding-agent reliability as a dependency chain: measurement and grading validity constrain what containment/recovery engineering can claim, which constrains what retrieval/context and human-review layers can be trusted to do, down to allocation and cost. Contributes a versioned catalog of 206 reliability records (193 gated practices, 13 research leads).

paper:2026arXiv260814131R.takeaway: Demonstration-derived prompts (generated from a single expert screen recording) are compared against expert-crafted procedural prompts under the same fixed task contract, testing whether procedures reconstructed from video approximate hand-written ones.

paper:2026arXiv260818092Y.takeaway: Argues the standard MAS failure taxonomy is cut along the wrong axis: failures filed as coordination or communication breakdowns are classical concurrency anomalies over shared mutable state. Four are named and worked through -- stale read (agent A reads utils.py, reasons for a minute, and writes main.py importing a function B renamed in the interim), lost update (two agents edit different parts of one file from the same base version, the later write silently discards the earlier), stale correction (a plan correction is broadcast but not applied atomically, so a third agent executes the superseded plan), and action-message desynchronization (an agent acts on a message describing world state another agent already invalidated). The tabulated re-attribution: premature submission 37.2% and consensus failure 29.9% on Silo-Bench, inter-agent misalignment 36.9% on MAST, against reported MAS failure rates of 41% to 86.7% overall.

paper:2026arXiv260818167Q.takeaway: A direct measurement of whether adding reviewing agents helps. On LiveCodeBench, zero-shot, self-refine, one reviewer and two reviewers sit indistinguishably at 75-77% pass; the five-agent MARS configuration reaches 82%; the three-agent Adversarial Review reaches 87%, the highest with the fewest agents among methods that broke out of the cluster. The failure mode that appears when the structure is added without discipline is false consensus: on SWE-PRBench naive AR drops to F1 0.457, below every non-interacting baseline, because the reviewer hedges and the critic confirms, or the critic yields to a confident-sounding rebuttal that cites no code. Forcing the critic into a three-way verdict where disagreement must either cite contradicting code or be answered with code lifts the same structure to F1 0.533. The cost is recorded rather than assumed: AR spends about 4.5x zero-shot's tokens for its 3.6-point SWE-bench Verified gain.

paper:2026arXiv260818423W.takeaway: Grades memory by what it buys over 20 simulated years rather than by recall on planted facts. The engine accumulates every quantity into one composite score at every stop, with no LLM judge or human rater in the loop, and the scalar is then decomposed into six behavioral capabilities of which memory curation is one. Three capabilities track the score on every seed: reducing slow-payoff investment as the horizon ends (Spearman -0.58), keeping cash deployed rather than idle (-0.50), and opening contract renewals early (+0.45). Token spend is uncorrelated with score under every accounting the paper runs. Baselines are honest rather than decorative: across three seeds all 15 frontier models complete every horizon while the blind scripted anchors, including a disciplined heuristic, die out in 7 of their 9 runs, and a scripted upper anchor allowed to read the hidden state scores 95.54 against the best model's 90.94. The solo track plays each model against a frozen scripted world and the Arena places all 16 seats in one shared persistent economy, where the league title rotates among ten models and mid-board solo standings do not survive adaptive rivals.

paper:2026arXiv260818575L.takeaway: Attributing a multi-agent failure to a specific agent and error type is cheap if you stop treating it as a reasoning task. AFANet scores agent-level and pair-level (agent plus error type) attribution from a turn graph using a 65K-parameter GCN, matching or beating prompted, fine-tuned, and proprietary LLM baselines on average while cutting inference from 199-367s to 1.16s. The measurement context matters as much as the method: a random baseline averages 4.08 across the six reported metrics, pre-trained LLMs land between 10.12 and 15.85, and proprietary models including o3 and Gemini-2.5-Pro reach only 20.24 and 18.35 -- so every system in this comparison is closer to chance than to solved.

paper:2026arXiv260819564L.takeaway: 140 primary scenarios split deterministically 70/70 into development and held-out by sorted identifier within category, plus a separate 70-item contrast extension frozen before inference containing 35 evidence-flip pairs including seven cue-conflicting traps. Each item is an acquire context, a candidate update and a later reuse context, labeled with one of four actions: persist, ephemeral, verify, clarify. Coverage is 20 items each across stable preferences, episodic preferences, freshness-sensitive facts, one-off corrections, policy constraints, ambiguous updates and noisy failures, and the audited test distribution is 38 persist, 40 ephemeral, 33 verify, 29 clarify. Every category contains multiple actions, so the category is not the label, and eight lexical traps place words such as always or today in contexts where their usual heuristic action is wrong. A second track, MCB-Act, removes the label vocabulary entirely and requires one structured call among memory_write, use_now, check_source and ask_user, each with a required argument checked by deterministic minimum-content and relevance rules. Reference systems include always-persist, a majority-action predictor and a keyword heuristic, all of which sit at 0.257 to 0.314 accuracy.

paper:2026arXiv260819652F.takeaway: 234 multi-session scenarios across research, shopping and personal finance, in two length regimes: Set A holds 190 single-probe scenarios of 18 sessions each (median 165 turns, roughly 3k tokens), and Set B holds 44 scenarios fusing three trap threads of different failure modes into one conversation of about 38 sessions (median 599 turns, 3.6x Set A in turns, roughly 7k to 15k tokens) probed by a three-part question, for 322 graded probes in total. Scenarios are not hand-written. Each is generated as a symbolic event program of typed state operations (rule declarations, value updates, scoped exceptions, commitments, retractions) over ground, derived and declared state, and the gold answer is computed by replaying that program through a deterministic evaluator. A scenario is admitted as a trap exactly when one or more executable lazy-reader heuristics disagree with full replay, and the disagreeing policies become its failure-mode signature, yielding status, salience, sequence and compound traps plus anti-trap scenarios where the anchored answer is the correct one. A strong LLM renders each program into dialogue but supplies only surface vocabulary, and the pipeline programmatically verifies that every load-bearing fact appears in its assigned session and that no banned phrase leaks, re-rendering scenarios that fail.

paper:2026arXiv260820622J.takeaway: Authorization lives outside the harness, in a tool gateway. Instead of one hand-built method per anticipated operation, each backend registers a credential broker: the gateway authenticates the caller against the target system and returns one narrowly scoped token, against which the model composes its own Graph query, OData filter, or SQL through a single generic request tool. Risk is call-scoped and self-declared rather than a static tier on a tool: the model must set a risky boolean on every call, judged from the params it just constructed, and a call omitting it is rejected before reaching a backend. A risky call spawns a fresh sub-harness to judge it, on the argument that the context that composed a call should not grade it, and escalates to a blocking human approval queue only when that judge cannot clear it. Retrieval is a git-mirrored plain-text copy of the document stores, each file carrying its source ACL group and each sync cycle one commit.

paper:2026arXiv260821867W.takeaway: Retrieval is scored in two channels over the same bank. A hybrid retriever combines BM25 and embedding cosine similarity over a record's title, description and content, and the verifier descriptor then adjusts that score: quality and confidence raise it, staleness and overgeneralization penalties lower it, and records still marked provisional are held back from injection. Records routed to the failure-guard pool get their own retrieval score and are rendered in a separate block of the injected prompt, so the agent reads them as constraints on what not to do rather than as strategies to imitate.

paper:2026arXiv260823635Z.takeaway: Clean tool-calling accuracy hides almost all of the risk. Across 7 models, 16 sampled deterministic local tools, 4 perturbation families, 14 subtypes, and 15,456 single-family records, mean clean success is 0.979 with three models at 1.000, while overall robustness under perturbation runs 0.664 to 0.766. The damage is not spread evenly across the pipeline: averaged over models, tool-interface perturbation costs least at 0.918, then user-intent at 0.773 and runtime-environment at 0.688, while tool-output/observation perturbation collapses to 0.455 with no model above 0.60. The hardest single subtype is C2 return-evidence loss at 0.142, and it is not an artifact of unsolvable tasks: 34.0% of C2 instances are solved by at least one model, and a human annotator judged the clean answer recoverable from the perturbed return in 68.3% of an audited 60. Combined stress is worse than the worst of its parts. Across five mixed-family pairs, mean success is 0.448 at medium severity against 0.621 for the weaker isolated constituent and 0.754 for the mean of both, and 0.200 against 0.292 and 0.507 at heavy severity, so composite difficulty cannot be approximated by taking the minimum of two single-axis scores.

paper:2026arXiv260824060B.takeaway: Two results bound how much fusion and precision are worth. First, a coarse-to-fine cascade is free at the top of the ranking: reranking the top 1000 Hamming candidates at int8 or float32 precision yields identical P@10 and nDCG@10 to three decimals as an exhaustive scan at that precision on all eight datasets, diverging only in AP where documents below rank 1000 still count. The binary first stage already places every document a full-precision scan would rank in the top ten inside its top 1000, so Hamming plus int8 cosine matches exhaustive int8 at roughly one-fifth the latency (164.5 versus 822.5 ms). Second, reciprocal rank fusion is not a safe default. RRF is the best scrydb configuration on exactly one of eight datasets, Touche, where RRF over full-precision embeddings reaches 0.414 nDCG@10 against a 0.359 MTEB baseline; on the other seven it trails the better of the two rankings it fuses. Semantic retrieval over the binarized index beats BM25 on nDCG@10 on all eight datasets, so the two channels being fused are usually not of comparable strength.

paper:2026arXiv260824188S.takeaway: End-to-end on all 300 SWE-bench Lite instances, context compresses to 25.7% of its original size against 50.2% for a gpt-4.1-mini compressor and 61.9% for gpt-5, while retaining 86.5% of uncompressed single-shot solve quality. Run instead in the cat -n line-numbered regime real agents produce, the same 300 instances compress to 27.8% and retain 89.3%, and there the paired comparison is the informative one: 30 instances solved only uncompressed, 17 only compressed, an exact McNemar p=0.079. The authors state that this harness measures comprehension under compression, not end-to-end agent cost. Cost is argued separately: the model is a 264 MB LoRA adapter that self-hosts on a single 24 GB GPU with no per-token compressor fee, and at list prices gpt-5 used as a compressor is net-negative, costing more to run than the downstream tokens it saves.

paper:2026arXiv260824252H.takeaway: SA-Bench scores paper-to-code reproduction without running the code. Each of 30 ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2025 papers is decomposed into Semantic Alignment Units, atomic implementation claims that must be localizable to a concrete paper span, verifiable by static code inspection, and independently assessable; 1,491 survive human review, and roughly 17% of agent-extracted candidates are rejected outright, with recurring rejection patterns including prior-work contamination and reported result values mistaken for implementation requirements. Each SAU is scored on a five-level rubric (1.0 faithful, 0.75 minor deviation, 0.5 key omission, 0.25 core substitution, 0 absent) by a GPT-5.5 judge that first searches the repository for evidence and filters out claims with no code-level support. On 200 manually re-checked claims the judge matched the human score about 87% of the time, with disagreement concentrated on the D2 boundary between core mechanism present but incomplete and core mechanism missing.

paper:2026arXiv260824804E.takeaway: StarHarness holds model weights fixed and searches the executable scaffold around them: prompt and task framing, tool definitions and schemas, argument preprocessing, skills, MCP providers, subagent structure, context management, verification, and finish logic. The evolution pool is stratified by baseline failure mode (wrong_tool, context_loss, missing_evidence, premature_conclusion), baseline score, and verifier pass rate, then split into proposer-visible search tasks and proposer-hidden selection tasks with matched distributions, leaving a holdout that never touches proposal or acceptance. Twenty-one patches were accepted in total: 4 on ITBench, 12 on EnterpriseOps-Gym, 5 on AutomationBench. ITBench went from 40.0% to 75.0% with false positives falling from 0.79 to 0.33 and true positives rising from 0.45 to 0.78; EnterpriseOps-Gym went from 23.3% to 43.7% with verifier pass rate rising from 34.5% to 72.8%; AutomationBench went from 57.1% to 83.2% with tasks incurring guardrail violations falling from 20 to 4 and zero-score tasks from 24 to 6. Held-out gains were +31.7, +15.1, and +29.3 percentage points. The frozen harness, evolved once with GPT-5.4, improved every transferred model across GPT and Qwen families without re-evolution, by +10.7 to +46.3 points. The accepted edits fall into three kinds: interface repair (stripping null and placeholder arguments before they reach a strict MCP server, preserving compound schemas), environment conventions made explicit (coupled priority and impact updates, preserving relationship fields, anchoring relative dates to the sandbox clock), and operational knowledge that compresses search (a forensics overview ranking candidate upstream causes, deterministic date and finance calculators).

paper:2026arXiv260824979S.takeaway: FrontierChallenge curates 300 end-to-end scientific workflows and releases 97 of them across quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment, then runs twelve frontier models across three scaffolds (Codex, Claude Code, Frontier Agent). Pass Rate, the fraction of tasks satisfying the complete deliverable contract, ranged from 3.1% to 20.6% while Avg. Score ranged from 67.5 to 87.9; the two best configurations, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex and Grok 4.6 with Claude Code, each completed 20 of 97 tasks. The divergence is worst where partial credit looks best: analytical chemistry reached an Avg. Score of 87.6 with a top Pass Rate of 4%, and electrochemistry/environment reached 94.9 with a Pass Rate of 0% for every configuration. Two behavioral signals fail as completion evidence. Of 849 non-passing Claude Code trajectories, 641 (75.5%) ended with a final message claiming completion and only 13 (1.5%) said work was still running. Raw tool errors were more common in passing runs than failing ones (94.2% versus 80.7% of trajectories; medians 5.6 versus 4.4 errors per 100 tool results), so an error count identifies neither the contract breach nor the successful run.

paper:2026arXiv260825091Z.takeaway: The paper makes inter-agent messages themselves the untrusted surface. A peer's natural-language subtask can carry an unverifiable permission claim, and with no receiver-side guard the NL manager-to-peer condition wrongfully actuates on 60/60 Borrowed Authority requests, identical to the plain Skill baseline where the model is the only filter. Edge Skillguard requires the receiving policy to satisfy typed contracts before a transition: the lease issuer must be the root agent, its grantee must equal the broker-attested envelope sender_id, its scope must contain the requested action, its base_commit must match the current commit, the presence source must be in {phone, cam, button}, and the presence observation must be under 30 seconds old, with deny conditions for vacation and lockdown modes. That drops wrongful actuation to 0/60 across five variants without blocking any of 60 benign requests, at 3.2 microseconds median in-process, 273 microseconds over a local broker, and 5.7 ms cross-host over Tailscale. The layer depends on five substrate preconditions it does not itself provide: schema-validated typed envelopes with closed-enum message types and an A2A v1.0 task-state lifecycle, broker-attested sender_id taken from the connection token rather than the payload, durable per-agent FIFO inboxes, an audit-mirror outbox giving every cross-agent action two independently attested write points, and boundary rejection of malformed envelopes with no silent translation of legacy fields.

paper:2026arXiv260825322Y.takeaway: Authority is enforced at one gate under a fixed precedence rather than at each call site. A permission decision returns allow, ask or deny after checking the plan boundary, then bypass-immune safety and secret-read checks, then rules resolved by authority and recency, then path scope, and only then the mode fallback, so a stale allow cannot authorize a mutation after a mode change. Interactive approval, protocol permission replies and headless policy all terminate at that same gate, and built-ins, plugin tools and MCP tools resolve through one registry before dispatch, which is the property that matters because equivalent effects routed through different tools would otherwise traverse different checks. Batch preflight requires every pending ask in a batch to resolve before the first admitted effect begins, and a denied call receives a typed error result so refusal does not leave a hole in the next request. A route-level oracle with one authorized and one unauthorized handcrafted decision for each of five routes (built-in write, Bash, alias, MCP, plugin-loaded MCP) matched all ten with no false positives or negatives, calling only the decision function and never executing an effect. In the child ablation, the cloned gate plus plan-filtered registry blocked the declared unauthorized effect and left 0 of 5 escape tools visible; removing both admitted the effect and exposed 5 of 5. Explicit bypass mode is documented as failing open after the hard checks, and optional worktree isolation separates repository writes only, not network access, provider state, host resources or credentials.

paper:2026arXiv260825403M.takeaway: A code study puts production practice close to the worst case the model predicts, and its own error bars are part of the result. Of 200 popular Python microservice repositories, regex-based static analysis detected explicit retry logic in 23 (11.5%, Wilson interval plus or minus 4.4pp), but a seeded audit of 30 repositories with no detection found retry logic in 10, a 33.3% false-negative rate that puts true prevalence near 41% (28.5% to 56.8%), mostly hand-rolled attempt loops. Cleaning mattered as much as detection: of 162 raw hits, 41 lay under example, documentation, playground, benchmark or integration-test paths, with one resilience library contributing 13 from a docs snippets directory illustrating every backoff variant it ships, and 8 more were duplicate detections of a single policy, leaving 113 production configurations. The original jitter rule credited jitter whenever the words jitter or random appeared nearby; opening all eight positives left three genuinely randomizing constructs, two of them documentation snippets, so exactly one configuration in 113 randomizes its delay. Retry counts above five are the largest group at 43.8% of the 73 that state one, immediate retry with no delay accounts for 31.0%, every configuration is static at deploy time, and none of the 23 projects coordinates retry decisions across a service boundary. The five anti-patterns are counted per project against a base of 23, so their intervals run to plus or minus 18pp and the authors mark the figures indicative rather than definitive.

paper:2026arXiv260825960C.takeaway: Retrieval over the memory store is two-channel, and the channels measurably do different jobs. A stored experience is scored against the current query as a convex combination of query-embedding cosine similarity and cosine similarity between the current query's base entity activation vector and the stored sparse activation map, so surface query similarity and evidence-neighborhood proximity remain separate signals rather than one embedding. The top-K activation maps are then fused into the retriever's initial activation vector, which means memory changes where graph propagation begins rather than being appended to the prompt; the rest of the backbone, sentence-entity propagation and Personalized PageRank over the passage-entity graph, is untouched, and the system falls back to the base retriever when the store is empty or the query yields no seed entities. Scaffold selection adds a third signal that retrieval deliberately omits, masked-template similarity, because a scaffold only enters the prompt and cannot inject historical entities into graph retrieval. A motivating measurement justifies the split: across five streams, direct entity overlap with an earlier query ranges from 4.30% on 2Wiki to 76.69% on WixQA, so an entity-keyed cache would miss most opportunities, while graph-neighborhood overlap runs 80.45% to 99.70%. Added per-query cost is linear in store size and independent of the corpus graph size, since only the top-K maps are fused.

paper:2026arXiv260900050S.takeaway: The agent harness is a zero-trust boundary enforced per action rather than per session: workload identity, least-privilege authorization, policy-scoped tool access through MCP, tenant isolation, and sandboxed execution split by action type, with VS Code and Chrome sandboxes for repository and browser work and a gVisor-isolated GKE Agent Sandbox for deployment and verification. Under the authorization-policy condition, all four models denied 140/140 unauthorized or out-of-scope capability requests before invocation and permitted 139/140 matched authorized requests. Both figures were identical from Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite to GPT-5.6 Sol, and held at 100% denial across all 14 domains with a lowest-domain permission rate of 90.0%.

paper:2026arXiv260901870Y.takeaway: Fan-out of independent rollouts does not close the gap: majority voting over N single-agent runs saturates at 63.5 percent at N=40 on BrowseComp-Plus, while ArcticSwarm reaches 82.6 at a token-matched budget. The failure it targets is premature consensus: on GPT-5 runs, questions where the orchestrator never opened an alternative or contrarian task scored 26.8 percent against 91.4 when at least one ran, across every difficulty tier. Ablating gated isolation on the shared board costs 3.8 points; removing the three review gates in turn (commit gate, board audit, self-check) drops accuracy monotonically by 6.3 points, and removing both mechanisms lands at 74.5. Communication-mode swaps holding model, timeout and tools fixed show single-agent and direct-messaging conditions well below the gated board, so structured coordination rather than agent count drives the gain.

paper:2026arXiv260901873B.takeaway: Spawning another agent is not obtaining another observation. A report Z is defined as an epistemic Sybil extension relative to already-admitted reports R when it adds no conditional information about the latent state, I(Theta; Z | R) = 0, however different its identity, wording, argument or computational path. The paper establishes a report-only identification barrier: the same observable report profile can descend from replicated ancestry or from independent corroboration and warrant different Bayes-optimal updates, so no aggregator working from report content alone can generally distinguish replication from corroboration. In more than 20,000 controlled LLM-agent calls on synthetic evidentiary documents, holding one evidence root fixed while report multiplicity rises from 1 to 32 collapses naive posterior coverage from 0.940 to 0.263; raising the number of genuinely independent roots from 1 to 16 closes the gap, with the aggregators statistically indistinguishable at k = 16.

paper:2026arXiv260902371B.takeaway: The paper supplies a ten-mode failure taxonomy organized by where the failure manifests in a trajectory. Reasoning failures are Wrong Context (context that is irrelevant, invalid or misleading), Instruction Unfollowing, Insufficient Context (essential information missing from the input) and Context Miss (relevant history overlooked). Control-flow failures are Termination Miss (execution continues past completion), Premature Termination and Step Loop. Action failures are Action Mismatch, Invocation Issue and Execution Failure. Each mode is formalized as a neural invariant violation rather than left as a descriptive label, and the framework extends to new taxonomies by adding violation conditions. The taxonomy also generates AgentErrata, a new dataset built by taxonomy-guided fault injection.

paper:2026arXiv260907360K.takeaway: Measures the agent configuration layer as a supply chain. Across 3,171 public GitHub repositories, 2,660 full agent setups and 511 component collections, 31 rules are applied at file, filesystem and pairwise scope; no pairwise or setup-level rule survives validation. Validation is three-stage and fully automated: an independent re-implementation re-derived 8,547 findings across 1,115 re-cloned repositories, 744 disagreeing pairs went to an LLM adjudicator with 586 already in agreement and 640 counted as defects, and a second independent model session re-read all 743 counted pairs, with no human scoring anywhere. Six rules reach the gating tier. Per-setup prevalence: unpinned MCP package 9.8%, a skill that pre-approves shell 3.8%, an arbitrary-execution grant such as Bash(python:*) 3.1%, skill without frontmatter 2.3%, missing agent description 0.8%, missing skill description 0.2%, committed local settings 0.7% as provisional. Aggregates: any security defect 16.0% with a 14.6-17.4 interval, any confirmed defect 16.7% at 15.4-18.2, any confirmed finding 18.4% at 17.0-19.9, against 25.5% from the raw gate output before the audit. Collections are cleaner at 3.7% shipping a shell-pre-approving skill and 6.8% carrying any confirmed finding.

paper:2026arXiv260908149Z.takeaway: The repair is mechanical rather than advisory. Repository reconstruction rebuilds each task as a fresh single-commit repository, on the finding that the common proposal of deleting branch, remote and tag refs still leaves the objects recoverable from .git/objects through notes, replace refs and stashes. Test artifacts are concealed and git hooks disabled; metadata passes an allowlist filter with instance-ID hashing and repository names stripped from paths; the network blocks GitHub raw and API endpoints plus GitLab, Gitee, Bitbucket, Codeberg and GitCode. Task refinement is a separate pass: 119 candidates drawn from public issue reports went through LLM filtering and draft fixes, then minimal human expert revision, producing 102 refined and 17 rejected, with defect categories of misleading description 22, overly narrow test 75, overly broad test 3 and other 2. The released benchmark is 731 instances.

paper:2026arXiv260908279S.takeaway: Separates memory that was destroyed from memory that was merely not retrieved. The restore counterfactual reinstates a question's gold evidence and reruns the frozen reader, giving a restore gain in minus one, zero, one and an irreversible-loss indicator that fires only when the gold evidence is absent from the surviving store, which sorts oracle-answerable policy errors into irreversible, recoverable and residual. On LongMemEval-S with 470 evidence-labeled questions over roughly 102k-token histories at 8k, 30k and 80k budgets, the two-bin irreversible share at 80k under top-k retrieval is 0.71 for FIFO (0.61-0.81), 0.73 random, 0.67 redundancy-aware and 0.60 for LLM-importance, whose interval straddles 0.5; a destructive information-density control that evicts gold about three times as often sits at 1.00, as do all four policies at 8k. Question type splits it: single-session questions are roughly 95% irreversible, while multi-session and temporal questions carry 23-34% residual. A slack audit over 2,276 irreversible cases finds that restoring only surviving gold reclassifies 0.3% and restoring the full retained store recovers 2%, so 98% is genuine destruction, against a placebo restore that flips 8.3% where gold flips 100%.

paper:2026arXiv260908371S.takeaway: The argument is structural: a single task-scoped policy has to grant the union of everything the task needs, so the runner that reads poisoned tool output also holds the patcher's write authority. CapScope moves authorization out of the model's context into a host-side reference monitor. A preflight model call sees only the trusted user request and the project file tree, names and never contents, mints a task-wide authority ceiling that deterministic host code validates and compiles, and the ceiling is frozen before any repository content or tool output is read and kept outside the model's context. A capability pairs an effect with a scope predicate: Read and Write over canonicalized path prefixes with .. and symlinks resolved, Exec over parsed argument-vector prefixes with compound commands split per segment and redirections removed. Three rules govern the store: Mint only from trusted policy, Derive a sub-agent store as a structurally contained subset, Invoke only when a held capability covers the effect. Over 4 conditions by 5 Python repair tasks by 5 injection surfaces by 3 trials, 300 runs, injected effects execute in 47/75 runs under ambient authority, 46/75 under a static denylist, 33/75 under a task-specific global policy and 3/75 under CapScope, with task success at 68/75 against 72/75 for the ambient baseline.

paper:2026arXiv260908589W.takeaway: The failure is structured rather than noisy, and it lives in the nonterminal states. Across seven StageIF deployments the terminal-minus-nonterminal adherence gap is significant for six and spans 29.4 to 89.3 points: qwen3.5-35b-a3b runs 21.7/1.2/2.9/97.9 across Wait, Ready, Step and Done for a gap of -89.3, qwen3.5-122b-a10b 83.5/0.0/0.0/66.2 for -38.4, and only gpt-5.5 at 57.7/58.2/34.5/54.4 has a confidence interval covering zero. The most extreme deployment reports correctly at 97.4% terminal against 8.2% intermediate. On deployments whose worst stage is mid-task, 82-90% of well-formed mid-task errors name a pre-action state the run has already left and 10-18% prematurely claim completion; on three collapsing deployments 44-67% of multi-checkpoint trajectories have every mid-task report wrong against 0-4% entirely correct. Interventions do not close it: supplying the true stage or a constant value leaves an upper interval below one sixth of the observed gap, a trailing reminder's largest pooled gain is 9.3 points, and reasoning mode redistributes failures instead of removing them. Withdrawing a needed tool and assigning the unfinished step elsewhere, with task truth unchanged, raises false completion from 6.2% to 64.4% across nine deployments.

paper:2026arXiv260911028Z.takeaway: The lifecycle is written as a finite TLA+ model with seven integrity dimensions. Six are structural invariants checked with TLC; the seventh, whether the test measures what it claims, is recorded and not enforced. A phase-aware static taint analysis over the task package and runtime lifecycle checks feed an audit agent with pinned evidence. Against BenchJack on the same tasks and model, full-chain recall rises from 23 to 94 percent up to 77 to 100 percent, and cost per task falls on all three benchmarks, for example from $5.91 to $2.05 on Terminal-Bench 3.

paper:2026arXiv260911076H.takeaway: SaltBench is a protocol for measuring what a working method costs when a machine referee decides the outcome. The referee (a proof kernel, a verifier or a withheld test suite) sits outside the agent's toolchain. The agent is walled off from the network, reference solutions and the harness, and probes test the wall before scored runs. Predictions are frozen in advance, and hitting the budget is a halt, not a failure.

paper:2026arXiv260911286G.takeaway: A five-value specification (industry, size, business model, application portfolio and seed) produces one entity graph for a fictional company, projected into 66 product simulators such as Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Jira and Stripe over vendor REST and MCP interfaces. Each simulator rebuilds the graph from the seed, so the same customer, employee and deal agree across systems by construction. A 20,000-employee company comes to about 250,000 records, generated in about nine minutes.

paper:2026arXiv260911515S.takeaway: The benchmark generates a four-source data fabric (a PostgreSQL warehouse, a MongoDB store, a rate-limited mock SaaS API and documents) as a timeline with an append-only ground-truth ledger. Gold answers are computed from the ledger with no model in grading. An answer that is wrong at evaluation time but correct as of the agent's effective retrieval time counts as a freshness error; wrong at both counts as a reasoning error.

paper:2026arXiv260925396X.takeaway: Two agents working in parallel can each produce a patch that passes its tests and merges cleanly, and the combination still fails. The paper measures this as tests that pass with each patch alone and fail merged, with the same test set in every condition. On 36 constructed tasks over 12 real Django helpers, GPT-5.5 working blind shows this interference in 105 of 108 runs. A short message describing the other agent's change recovers 89 of 108.

paper:2026arXiv261000371Z.takeaway: Fragments that each pass a local check can combine into a prohibited use. With artifacts, policy and proposal held fixed, per-artifact review permits 413 of 480 denied commits (86.0 percent) and reviewing the union permits none, with 459 of 480 authorized objects supplied in both arms. The paper counts a control as successful only when it blocks the prohibited use and completes the paired authorized one. Class-only review withholds most denied values but achieves zero joint successes. Binding review to resolved objects, with deterministic enforcement at a commit gate, reaches 96.5 to 99.7 percent selective correctness with no verbatim release across 2,304 trials.

paper:2026arXiv261000648F.takeaway: The paper sorts 1,948 failed trials into exclusive causes. The repair did not last in 26.5 percent, the agent declared while the service was still out of bounds in 23.9 percent, it changed something off the permitted list in 21.9 percent, it never declared in 16.3 percent, and it left the planted cause or damage in place in 8.7 percent. Of 2,967 episodes with an action record, 55 percent issued the full reference fix and only 59 percent of those passed. Among the 672 that had the full fix and still failed, 340 declared before the service recovered and 329 failed a safety check by undoing their own fix.

paper:2026arXiv261000905R.takeaway: The study reads 944 closed GitHub issues, filtered from 22,848 across 21 open-source multi-agent projects, and codes each for the issue, its cause and its solution. Orchestration and execution problems are the largest category at 22.0 percent, followed by memory and state management at 14.7 percent. Tool issues are 9.2 percent, and model issues only 1.6 percent.

paper:2026arXiv261000972Z.takeaway: On pools of ten rollouts of Claude Opus 4.8 on APEX-Agents, 34 percent of the 917 claims the rollouts agree on are wrong. Of 775 disputed claims, 74 percent contain a correct candidate, but the most frequent answer is correct in only 47 percent. Across five benchmarks, majority voting over ten rollouts moves the average score from 47.2 to 47.5 with Gemini 3.5 Flash and from 49.6 to 50.4 with Opus. VeriHarness, which checks competing and shared claims against files, data and constraints in the workspace, reaches 51.6 and 53.7 by selection and 53.4 and 56.1 with evidence-backed revision.

paper:2026arXiv261007261M.takeaway: Each agent passes its own checks on its own branch while the merged tree is broken. NP-Bench reads the outcome off a real git merge and test run (does the merged tree build, does it pass, did the consumer adapt to the new contract) across three arms: no coordination, reactive detection and proactive planning.
