With live agents on a breaking contract change, the clean-integration rate is 0 under no coordination and 0 under reactive detection on every seed. The planner raises it to 1.0 on a frontier model and 0.6 on a small one, and none of 5 agents strayed from its assigned scope. A separate cross-session memory test drops the repeated-mistake rate from 1.00 to 0.00 on both a strong and a weak model.

paper:2026arXiv261007309W.takeaway: The paper adds a question to memory evaluation that retrieval-correctness and answer-correctness both miss: was the retrieved record eligible for this principal, purpose, intent and time. It audits each retrieved record at matched required-evidence recall, tracks the memory ID through prompt exposure, and scores target-level disclosure in the answer. On frozen rankings from RHELM and MemOps (3,767 queries), trusted-namespace filtering raises top-20 anchor recall from 0.432 to 0.533 and the share of queries where 80 percent recall is feasible from 0.237 to 0.311, with 98.3 percent fewer exact similarity evaluations.

paper:2026arXiv261007639Z.takeaway: The study assesses 40 coding agent harnesses, 27 open-source and 13 closed-source, against a taxonomy of ten security mechanisms. Of the 400 harness-mechanism cells, 205 are confirmed implemented, 83 are confirmed absent and 112 stay unresolved. About half of the confirmed implementations are opt-in, and the evidence gaps sit mostly in closed-source products. HarnessSecurity-Bench then runs 23 coding tasks across five attack surfaces on Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, gptme, Qwen Code and GitHub Copilot with GLM-5.2 held fixed, 2,500 trials and 81,155 tool calls. Enabling auto-approve raises attack success from 29.2 to 95.6 percent. Network isolation cuts it from 57.1 to 0.8 percent and costs 24.5 points of task utility. Read-only mode cuts it from 8.3 to 0.8 percent and costs 34.0 points. Command allowlisting reduces attack effects at a small utility loss, and command denylisting reduces them with a utility gain.

paper:2026arXiv261010126L.takeaway: Failure type depends on communication topology. On the 851 MAST-clean traces, a contingency table of four topologies against the fourteen MAST failure modes rejects independence with chi-squared 409.9 and p of 1.2e-70. Giving a small judge the ground-truth topology and the failure patterns typical of it raises gpt-mini's Macro-F1 on failure classification from 0.173 to 0.350. The paper's worked example is a shared-message-pool run: a reviewer asks for interrupted-transfer handling in a file-transfer tool, the tester adds tests for an unrelated square function, and the next review accepts them.

paper:2026arXiv261010961X.takeaway: A second agent from another provider reviewing a finished turn is only a review if the runtime can show it received the complete input, produced a usable critique and ran in a separate resource pool. The paper states that as a six-property contract and finds three ways its own implementation counted a failed review as complete. A reviewer given truncated input returned a plausible clean verdict at four truncation levels, from 1 percent delivered to one character missing. Cancellation during process reaping was counted as a completed review. A reviewer that exited nonzero with a well-formed verdict was counted as complete, found only after preregistered collection had begun. In the 20-turn pilot, eight turns had a material reviewer finding (95% exact interval 19.1 to 63.9 percent).

paper:2026arXiv261011559D.takeaway: SWE-Journey generates both halves of its evaluation. Tasks come from a weak-to-strong synthesis pipeline that decomposes a long-horizon task into subtasks, synthesizes each subtask's components separately and accumulates a reusable module-level skills library, at $56.64 per task. Users come from four personas mined from real interaction data, Non-coder, Product Manager, New Developer and Software Architect, which condition a GLM-5.2 simulator that discloses requirements gradually and differs by persona in expertise, detail preference, control style, goal stability and verification style. The same assistants pass over 75 percent of tests for requested functionality with the Software Architect persona and fewer than 25 percent with the Non-coder.

paper:2026arXiv261012822H.takeaway: Reward hacks elicited by coding RL (exit-code manipulation, always-equal objects, conftest hooks against a leaky pytest evaluator) propagate from small open-weight sources to stronger closed-weight targets through shared code, shared memory and natural-language plans; a hacking planner induced confirmed hacks in every target coder, and some targets adopt the hack only after evaluator feedback, which evaluation of first submissions misses.

paper:2026arXiv261013065E.takeaway: 165 Rust, Go and C++ command-line applications from ProgramBench, each with a refined natural-language specification and about 74 requirement-targeted mutants that exactly one reference test kills, scored by test validity rate and mutation score.

paper:2026arXiv261013361W.takeaway: 25 commissions (10 Creation, 10 Editing on pinned OpenHands- and Aider-style codebases, 5 Optimization) in which a builder sees a few development cases and is graded on held-out cases with requirement-derived rubrics and hard zero gates; the best of five models in the Codex harness averaged 19.1 on Creation and 31.6 on Editing.

paper:2026arXiv261013889C.takeaway: EcoAgent indexes 5,172 tools from LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex and n8n and finds more than half flawed; a reliability score from name-description consistency, source credibility and documentation quality keeps 2,940 tools at 0.8 or above, and selection of faulty tools fell from 86.2% to 2.9% at a 30% injected failure rate.

paper:2026arXiv261017685C.takeaway: LatentRiskBench pairs each risky workflow with a benign twin that ends in the same terminal action, so only workflow state separates them: accumulated content, artifacts, outbound destination, approval status, data-sensitivity tags and alignment with the user's goal. An auditor that sees only the action detects 0.09 of violations; one that reconstructs state detects 0.96, a gap of 0.87 (McNemar p<1e-15). On the 124-trace core set, residual risk is 0.96 with no guard, 0.85 under LlamaGuard 3, 0.78 under keyword filters, 0.59 under step rules, 0.50 under trajectory rules, 0.32 under an LLM judge and 0.20 under GuardAgent.

paper:2026arXiv261018410S.takeaway: Five offline transformations fold a knowledge graph's neighbourhood into node embeddings (one-hop and two-hop blends, a retrofitting pull, random-walk endpoint blends, Louvain cluster blends) so a plain vector index can answer relational questions without walking the graph at query time. Replacing the original embeddings outright hurt, but using the modified embeddings in a second query stage helped: a chained requery over random-walk embeddings lifted recall on the hard relational and collection questions from 51.0 to 60.8 percent at a 40-node budget, and matched plain retrieval's 40-node recall with 24 nodes.

paper:2026arXiv261032060P.takeaway: Pitre et al. built a failure taxonomy from 3,211 failed multi-round debates over eight datasets (FinQA, HotpotQA, MBPP, MMLU-Pro, MedQA, MuSiQue, Ethics, LiveCodeBench) run on open-weight agents from LLaMA-3.2-3B to GPT-OSS-120B. Recovery/correction failures appear in 94.9% of failed trajectories and consensus/decision failures in 83.4%. Against 500 successful debates, reasoning and tool/evidence errors occur at the same rates (0.35 and 0.38 of failed trajectories, 0.35 and 0.39 of successful ones); what separates failure is recovery failure (0.94 against 0.37), persistent wrong framing (0.60 against 0.08) and premature consensus (0.71 against 0.20). 91.2% of successful debates still contained at least one error. Consensus errors rise in round 2, the first round after agents see each other's answers. Once they appear before the final round, persistent wrong framing, failure to recover after an unknown answer, and failed recovery after disagreement are still present at the end about 81% of the time.

paper:CharltonPerez2024Ciaran.takeaway: Compares learned and physical models on a single damaging windstorm and finds the learned models captured the synoptic evolution well while under-representing the near-surface wind extremes that caused the damage.

paper:Ebert2008Fuzzy.takeaway: Reviews neighborhood-based verification methods and organizes them by the decision model each implies, showing how a high-resolution forecast can be penalized by point matching while being more useful than a smooth one.

paper:GneitingCalibration2007.takeaway: Proposes the paradigm of maximizing sharpness subject to calibration, distinguishes probabilistic, exceedance and marginal calibration, and gives diagnostic tools including the PIT histogram.

paper:GneitingRaftery2007.takeaway: Develops the theory of scoring rules that are maximized only by reporting the true predictive distribution, covering CRPS, the logarithmic score, and the Brier score as instances of one framework.

paper:McGreivy2024.takeaway: Identifies two systematic failures in scientific machine-learning evaluation: baselines that are weaker than the state of the art in the target field, and a publication process that does not surface failed comparisons.

paper:OWASPLLM.takeaway: A community-maintained catalogue of the top LLM-application security risks — prompt injection, insecure output handling, excessive agency, supply chain, and more.

paper:SunGraySwan2024.takeaway: Removes the most intense cyclones from training and tests whether learned models can still forecast them, finding they cannot extrapolate to unseen intensity even though the governing physics is unchanged.
